claim.short: Per-mission decomposition of the pooled mouse-tissue proteostasis-11 signature used in PRs #7-#10. Of the six mouse tissues, only gastrocnemius shows both missions consistently translation-suppressed (RR-1 mean NES -2.04, RR-9 -2.47; range 0.42) with significant positive Spearman r against the human Inspiration4 skin anchor (r = +0.882 and +0.755, perm p = 0.001 and 0.008). Skin shows striking within-tissue heterogeneity (range 5.14): MHU-2_dorsal alone reproduces the gastrocnemius-like suppression (-2.23), while MHU-2_femoral (+1.85) and RR-6 (+2.91) are oppositely directed. Thymus, liver, kidney, and eye are predominantly translation-up across their missions, consistent with the anti-correlation observed in the pooled matrix.

inputs.notes: Same local mouse fGSEA cache as PRs #7-#10. Mission coverage: thymus (MHU-2, RR-6, RR-9), gastrocnemius (RR-1, RR-9), skin (MHU-2_dorsal, MHU-2_femoral, RR-6), eye (RR-1, RR-3, OSD-397/TBD), liver (MHU-2, RR-1, RR-3, RR-6, RR-8, RR-9), kidney (RR-1, RR-3, RR-7). 20 (tissue, mission) pairs total.

Used as the single human anchor for the Spearman r test (the cleanest cell in PR #10's matrix). All 11 proteostasis pathways are present in this compartment, so the per-mission Spearman is computed on n=11 each.

validation.notes: Exploratory local-only run. The per-mission Spearman is computed on n=11 pathways (the i4_skin set contains all 11 proteostasis pathways), so the test is not power-limited at n. The cross-mission stability claim is therefore a sound robustness check on PRs #7-#10's pooled signal. Promotion past exploratory still requires the same HPC c2cgp/c5bp re-run to lift the broader matrix coverage, and the i4_skin CSV needs registration in input_freeze.json (still outstanding from PR #7).
